text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Renel RA electricity authority plans to turn into a shareholding company and to launch Eurobonds in the international market in January.
- Finance Minister designate Mircea Ciumara said he believed the depreciation of the leu currency would come to a halt.
- Bankcoop SA commercial bank plans to increase its capital to 70 billion lei from 37 billion from dividends and money allotted to the development fund from profits.
- Renel got $160 million syndicated loan for fuel oil imports this winter.
ADEVARUL
- The liberalisation of the foreign exchange market is the basic solution for growing exports, the newspaper says.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Investment in road rehabilitation this year amounted to 300 billion lei.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Parliament's standing commissions accepted all 27 candidates proposed by Prime Minister-designate Victor Ciorbea for his centrist government. Parliament is expected to debate the proposals for the government team and its programme.
ADEVARUL
- President Emil Constantinescu to attend the summit of the European Union in Dublin starting December 15.
- Ciorbea to give up the job of Bucharest mayor next week.
- Resorts at the Black Sea need serious restructuring, says in interview Peter Shackleford, representative of the World Tourism Organisation.
- The leftist parties should unite, Tudor Mohora, head of the Socialist Party, says in interview.
LIBERTATEA
- Police and prosecution have no money to complete investigations in cases of corruption, the newspaper says.
COTIDIANUL

- Adrian Nastase, executive president of the Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), said his party will not approve Ciorbea's governing programme because it criticises the way the PDSR had ruled the country over the past four years.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- First private school for the children of Turkish businessmen living in Romania opened in Bucharest. ($=3,616 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
